## Engineering status — 2026-11-15

Phase 2 V18 is under final integration. Its frozen full suite, strict real
L1/L2/L3 runs and fifteen-goal acceptance audit are pending. Phase 2 completion
must not be inferred from local tests or a successful protocol probe.

V16 is retained as a failed historical boundary: 1,304 backend tests passed and
five failed, with one warning in 328.69 seconds. Its three strict live runs all
failed before plan approval, using 66,428 / 78,872 / 90,794 known tokens within
the original L1/L2/L3 totals. No Worker/review/restart occurred. See
[the V16 independent boundary](docs/audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v16-boundary.md).

V17 passed 1,405 frozen backend tests with one warning in 427.75 seconds, but
all three strict live runs failed at the pre-model Planner goal-size guard.
They used 4,233 / 4,366 / 4,844 known tokens, with only two settled calls per run,
no unknown usage and no Worker or review. Its complete historical source and
failures are retained in [the V17 boundary](docs/audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v17-boundary.md).

V17 integrates complete approved predecessor-delivery handoffs, independently
revalidated original PASS/lineage, native request/source capacity measurement
and explicit serial shared reserves. The original scenario totals and raw
65,536-byte review limit remain. Every successor needs its own execution and
fresh verification; unknown usage and held allocations are never refunded by
the serial policy. Automatic feedback can request a remaining-DAG proposal;
replacement plan and team approval remains required.

Local/Mock and scripted HTTP protocol checks are recorded separately from real
model results. One exploratory semantic-selection sample has an original false
oracle verdict and a separate independent source-binding interpretation; it
does not establish successful cross-Quest execution. The historical 90-row
single-model policy study contains 25 successes and 65 failures and supports no
broad dynamic-team superiority claim.

No new dependency or startup environment variable is introduced by these V17
changes. Desktop release and multimodal execution remain outside the verified
capability boundary. See [the report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md),
[status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and
[serial budget ADR](docs/adr/ADR-010-bounded-serial-review-reserve.md).

# V16 historical boundary and V17 draft

This is a draft for the integration owner. It does not replace the current README,
status, roadmap, quality-gate, experiments or Phase 2 report documents. V17 final
suite, frozen source, strict live runs and independent acceptance remain pending.

V16 finished with 1,304 backend tests passed, five failed and one existing
TestClient warning, over 328.69 seconds. The five failures are the retained
Planner wire-schema/lease/API compatibility regressions. Its 188-file manifest is
`e069c337d3d4cb5554181ef79a0f3803700b6e5d7f6c5a117dcb35d17c3f9cad`.

All three strict V16 live runs failed before plan approval. Each Router-created
Quest stayed proposed after five Planner inbox attempts and ten settled Planner
HTTP calls. The durable diagnostic is
`planning_failed:DomainError:Invalid_graph_proposal`; rejected model drafts and
their detailed validation digests were not saved, so a more specific root cause
cannot be inferred from these records. No Worker, Review PASS, revision,
mid-execution restart or context archive was produced. All 36 Gateway attempts
settled: L1 used 66,428/180,000 tokens, L2 78,872/360,000 and L3 90,794/630,000.
There are zero unknown final attempts, and each read-only database snapshot had
`total_changes=0`. See the complete `live-usage-v16-audit.json` and Markdown.

V17 adds an explicit, approved predecessor-delivery source contract. A node
declares `required_predecessor_deliveries`; the Core-owned
`worker_read_completed_delivery` accepts an explicitly approved success-path
ancestor node key. The original/current approved graphs and persisted edge rows
must agree, and one complete path through succeeded intermediate nodes must
connect that source to the reader. No shortcut edge is added to a serial chain.
It checks the reader's current approved node/member/tool scope and separately
revalidates the original succeeded predecessor through CompletionGate. Approved
remaining-DAG lineage can refer to the original run without rewriting its
receipts, counters, source artifacts or PASS hashes. Historical readers require
an exact succeeded run preserved by the actual current approved lineage.

The handoff contains the complete eight-field delivery plus its original
run/plan/result-event/hash binding. The delivery remains untrusted model claims.
Core enforces its original declared delivery byte bound and a whole-handoff cap
of 65,536 bytes; it never truncates the delivery. Worker tool selection, exact
arguments, Core call record and tool message must agree. A successful handoff is
a validated source for the successor, which must still run its own model,
produce its own result and obtain its own fresh independent PASS or declared
fixed verification. It does not need an unrelated file read merely to create an
action receipt.

Independent review includes the full handoff in `predecessor_deliveries`, only
when the new tool was actually used. Legacy packet hashes and wire formats stay
unchanged. Source-envelope accounting includes canonical receipts plus the full
canonical handoff list. Preview and capacity calculations must preserve the same
source bytes, native framing, unchanged raw packet cap and serial
review/correction reservation; neither a prediction nor a policy reserve counts
as actual Provider usage.

The original helper had 29 passing local tests (22.44 seconds), including real governed
files/fixed checks, original model-PASS hash tampering, current and inherited
readers, tool-message/assistant-call binding, byte limits and zero-mutation
reads. A wider review/context/capacity/Gateway/lineage regression passed 157 tests
in 61.94 seconds. One local scripted HTTP integration exercises the actual
Gateway/ledger and fresh-PASS-to-CompletionGate path for a read-only successor
without any new artifact or fabricated action receipt. It is an offline protocol
fixture and does not constitute live model-quality or strict Quest acceptance.
The final success-ancestor revision passed 35 cases in 27.19 seconds, adding a
real three-node chain without a shortcut edge plus nonancestor, non-success,
unfinished-path and persisted-edge rejection. Its first fixture attempt failed
six new cases due to a missing read tool scope; that failed attempt is retained.

Further V17 work owned by peers includes automatic feedback-triggered
`quest.replan_requested` consumption, approved remaining-DAG plans, bounded
hierarchical plans, selected-Provider capacity measurements, complete Core source
exchange archiving/readback and strict acceptance compatibility. Final text must
use frozen-source tests and actual live records for these features. Do not retain
the old V16 statement that no feedback path invokes remaining-DAG planning.

The controlled V16 algorithm study remains historical: 25/90 task successes and
65/90 failures, despite all model stages completing; 135 calls used 111,243 known
tokens. It used one model, six fixed cases and fifteen policy variants. Unequal
calls, independently sampled candidates and deterministic feedback prevent broad
claims about dynamic-team superiority. Its original failed rows, scores and
bounded-oracle results must be preserved.

Phase 2 completion remains gated on the final frozen suite, all strict current
L1/L2/L3 acceptance checks, required continuity observations and the fifteen-goal
evidence matrix. General task correctness, broad autonomous replanning quality,
multi-model selection quality and multimodal execution remain unproven. Typed
image/audio/video ingestion and execution are unavailable; explicit input-needed
handling is not multimodal execution. Unconfigured monetary cost remains unknown.

## Additional V17 evidence and pending integration

The explicit `serial-capacity-v1` policy is still under integration. It permits
only a connected success chain and approved concurrency one. Baselines, one
shared reserve and coordination must fit the original 180,000 / 360,000 / 630,000
scenario totals. Starting later nodes keeps held allocations and once-only
durable markers; unresolved Gateway attempts cannot be refunded or treated as
free capacity. Native start still protects future baselines and the current
complete review/correction cycle. The shared reserve may run out, in which case
the task truthfully blocks. An offline scripted HTTP two-node/reopen fixture
passed, with a separate tampered-capsule fixture rejected before HTTP. These
fixtures exercise the actual native Gateway and ledger, but not a real model.
ADR-010 records the policy. Core-measured resource derivation and final Planner
integration remain pending; no frozen-source or strict-live result is asserted.

One fixed exploratory semantic-retrieval call used the configured local proxy,
with one settled attempt and 1,826 known tokens. The original probe verdict is
false and retained: its oracle recorded four manually seeded candidate IDs while
automatic source sync added two literal global constraints. The model selected
three representations of the target user instruction; the oracle converted the
additional global constraint into a null ID and failed three checks. A separate
read-only independent audit rebuilt all six candidate records from actual source
rows, matched the exact live candidate snapshot SHA-256, rechecked both original
message row bytes/hashes, and resolved all three returned items to the target
message with their original trust preserved. Its eleven checks passed with zero
database changes. See `semantic-crossquest-v17-independent.json/.md`; never
rewrite the original false result. Two seeded Quests remain proposed. This is
bounded retrieval evidence for one sample, not successful cross-Quest execution,
general memory quality, source diversity or multi-model validation.

The prepared V17 usage auditor independently reconstructs held baseline and
serial-pool allocations, original scenario caps, stored start admission
snapshots, Gateway and local counters, unresolved reservations, complete review
packet/PASS bindings, completed-delivery handoffs and actual artifact hashes. It
uses SQLite URI read-only mode, `query_only`, explicit transactions and no Store
construction. The full independent acceptance auditor checks all fifteen goal
rows and the original frozen inventory/evidence, and will not promote successful
local fixtures or the semantic probe into strict L1/L2/L3 acceptance.

# Phase 2 — Experiments and Reproduction

Draft for final V18 integration, 2026-11-15. Frozen full-suite, strict current
L1/L2/L3 and final evidence inventory are pending. Original failed attempts stay
immutable and are included in the eventual publication index.

## Evidence categories

| Evidence | What it establishes | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local/Mock tests | Deterministic contracts, authority, budgets, failure handling and persistence | No real model quality |
| Scripted loopback HTTP | Actual native Gateway, attempt ledger and runtime protocol integration | Local scripted responses, even when the production adapter reports live mode |
| Real Provider protocol | Configured proxy returned supported dialogue/schema/tool/stream responses | Proxy success, upstream identity and correctness are separate claims |
| Real algorithm study | Fixed-case policy observations with independent bounded scoring | Small single-model sample; not autonomous Quest acceptance |
| Strict live Quest | Original scenario checks, actual evidence, continuity, budgets and current-source binding | A failed or partial run remains failed |

Historical reports and failed test attempts are retained under
`docs/audit/phase2/`; no later repair changes their original source identity.

## V16 historical boundary

Full backend suite: 1,304 passed, five failed, one warning, 328.69 seconds. The
retained failures concern Planner wire/schema/lease/API compatibility.
`source-manifest-v16.json` contains 188 files and canonical manifest SHA-256
`e069c337d3d4cb5554181ef79a0f3803700b6e5d7f6c5a117dcb35d17c3f9cad`.

| Strict run | Duration | Known tokens / original cap | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `20261115T082953Z-L1-16b57e` | 193.361 s | 66,428 / 180,000 | Failed before plan approval |
| `20261115T082953Z-L2-a68109` | 312.402 s | 78,872 / 360,000 | Failed before plan approval |
| `20261115T083313Z-L3-673598` | 373.787 s | 90,794 / 630,000 | Failed before plan approval |

Each run retained five Planner processing attempts, ten settled Planner HTTP
calls, one Router call and one semantic recall call. All 36 attempts settled,
with no Worker/review/archive/restart. Detailed rejected drafts were not saved;
`Invalid_graph_proposal` alone cannot identify a schema/capacity/model cause.
See [the immutable boundary](audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v16-boundary.md)
and [read-only usage audit](audit/phase2/live-usage-v16-audit.md).

## V17 local records

| Record | Result | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Final predecessor-delivery helper](audit/phase2/predecessor-ancestor-v17-second.xml) | 35 passed, 27.19 s | Full source/PASS/lineage/bytes plus actual three-node success-ancestor path and nonancestor/failure/unfinished/tampered path rejection; first failed fixture attempt retained |
| [Review/context/lineage group](audit/phase2/predecessor-review-lineage-v17-regression.xml) | 157 passed, 61.94 s | Overlapping local regressions; counts are not additive |
| [Native serial HTTP fixture](audit/phase2/serial-runtime-v17-final.xml) | 3 passed, 6.081 s | Actual Gateway/ledger with scripted responses; two nodes and Store reopen, cost/tamper failures before HTTP |

The V17 full frozen suite passed 1,405 tests with one warning in 427.75 seconds.
All three strict live runs failed before a Planner model call or Worker at
`Quest_is_too_large_to_plan`. Each retained five failed Planner inbox attempts
and two settled Router/semantic calls; there were no unknown attempts.

| Strict V17 run | Duration | Known tokens / original cap | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `20261115T092655Z-L1-c3a404` | 376.207 s | 4,233 / 180,000 | Entry guard failed |
| `20261115T092655Z-L2-350db9` | 376.101 s | 4,366 / 360,000 | Entry guard failed |
| `20261115T092655Z-L3-bf61b1` | 376.139 s | 4,844 / 630,000 | Entry guard failed |

The archived 201-file source independently matches its original manifest; this
is historical source, not current V18. See
[the V17 boundary](audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v17-boundary.md) and
[read-only usage audit](audit/phase2/live-usage-v17-audit.md). V18 entry-guard
repair, final frozen-suite and strict-live records remain pending.

## Fixed semantic retrieval sample

`.local/phase2/semantic-crossquest-v17-fixed-01/` preserves one fixed real call
with zero retries. Two prior Quests and two original user messages were seeded;
their status remained proposed. The Chinese query had no lexical index match to
the English target preference. The call settled at 1,713 input + 113 output =
1,826 tokens, with no unknown usage and unknown monetary cost.

The original `result.json` remains false. Its oracle only captured four manually
seeded candidate IDs, while source sync created two additional literal global
constraints. A selected global target constraint became null in that fixture's
lookup and caused three false oracle checks. Independent read-only inspection
rebuilt all six source records and matched the exact complete candidate snapshot
SHA-256 `713287d72f61f2db2664a222409c7a3c515a97e6c65ddd9e52f346cc66697789`.
All three returned records exactly matched the target source; both original
message rows and hashes were unchanged. All eleven independent checks passed,
with SQLite `total_changes=0`.

See [the separate immutable interpretation](audit/phase2/semantic-crossquest-v17-independent.md).
It neither rewrites the failed raw result nor establishes successful Quest
execution, broad memory quality, source diversity or multi-model capability.

## Historical controlled algorithm study

The retained V16 study has 90 rows, six fixed cases and fifteen policy variants.
It compares six team policies, five context policies and four governance
policies. Independent scoring found 25 task successes and 65 failures; all
stages completed. Its 135 calls used 91,487 input + 19,756 output = 111,243
tokens, with no unknown usage or score/hash/row discrepancies.

Unequal model calls, independently sampled candidates and deterministic failed
check feedback limit causal comparisons. One model and small fixed cases do not
establish dynamic-team superiority, model diversity or general task correctness.
The fixed oracle gate applies only to its stated cases. See
[results](audit/phase2/live-algorithm-study-v16-results.json) and
[independent audit](audit/phase2/live-algorithm-study-v16-independent.md).

## Reproduction and final acceptance

Use the native scripts under `backend/scripts/phase2/`. Provider calls pass
through the existing Gateway and durable model ledger. Credentials come only
from the existing local process configuration and never enter source or
reports. Do not modify the user's Provider service.

Strict scenarios retain 180,000 / 360,000 / 630,000 total tokens, the original
node/member/concurrency/duration/retry caps, full source criteria and the
65,536-byte raw review limit. Serial sharing is an explicit approved resource
policy with concurrency one; it does not demonstrate parallel execution.
Core-measured resource values require the normal plan and team approval.
Unknown/rejected-without-usage attempts keep their reservations.

Audit runtime databases with SQLite URI `mode=ro`, `PRAGMA query_only=ON` and an
explicit read transaction. Do not construct Store. The V17 usage auditor checks
original scenario caps, once-only reserve markers, held baseline allocations,
actual Gateway/local counters, full current review/PASS reconstruction, source
handoffs and artifact hashes. Final independent acceptance separately checks
the frozen inventory, full suite/static records, original evidence/test
preservation, published live snapshots and all fifteen goal rows.

Accepted results require actual current-source strict scenario success, required
source readback/context continuity and a real mid-execution Core process restart
where specified. Store reopen and after-completion restarts are narrower tests.

# Phase 2 — Agent Intelligence Report

Draft for final V18 integration, 2026-11-15. Phase 2 acceptance is pending the
frozen full suite, all strict current-source L1/L2/L3 checks and the fifteen-goal
matrix. This draft does not promote historical runs or local protocol fixtures.

FORGE retains one persistent user conversation. Router alone faces the user;
Planner, Workers and Reviewer execute privately through the native Core. No
Codex, DSH or Claude Code execution backend is used. Desktop release and UI work
are outside this sprint's acceptance target.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U[One user conversation] --> R[Persistent Router]
    R --> P[Planner: semantic DAG]
    P --> C[Core validation and capacity measurement]
    C --> A[User plan and team approval]
    A --> W[Native private Worker loop]
    W --> T[Governed tools and durable Gateway]
    T --> E[Receipts, full deliveries and source evidence]
    E --> V[Fresh independent Reviewer or declared fixed verifier]
    V -->|revision| W
    V --> G[NodeVerifier and CompletionGate]
    G --> R
    W -->|stopped failure with completed predecessors| P
```

The feedback path can request a remaining-DAG proposal. Core preserves completed
contracts, original runs, artifacts, counters and PASS hashes through explicit
lineage. A replacement plan and team still need approval. A proposal or source
handoff never proves successful execution.

## Implemented behavior and evidence limits

| Area | Implemented mechanism | Evidence boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Router and Planner | Typed decisions, source-bound constraints, separate semantic DAG planning, bounded repair and durable rejection diagnostics | Final V17 suite/live results pending; model reasoning quality is not established by schema compliance |
| Team selection | Capability eligibility, provenance-bearing observations, bounded dynamic roles and approved team contracts | Historical single-model microstudy; multi-model quality remains unproved |
| Resource admission | Actual native request framing, full source/output/review bounds and opt-in Core-measured serial resource allocation | Measurement is policy admission, not predicted usage or task success |
| Serial reserve | One strict success chain, concurrency one, node baselines and one shared contingency with durable once-only markers | Original scenario totals and Gateway caps remain; shared reserve can be exhausted |
| Native Worker | Private model/tool loop, leases, durable checkpoints, bounded self-repair and structured eight-field delivery | Local regressions plus separately recorded real Provider runs; strict V17 result pending |
| Evidence handoff | Explicitly approved success-path ancestor declaration and complete `worker_read_completed_delivery` source | Approved graph/persisted edges and succeeded path agree; full original live/fixed evidence is revalidated; delivery remains untrusted model claims |
| Independent review | Fresh context from original goal, current criteria, complete artifacts/receipts/handoffs and exact packet hash | Same approved underlying model; no independent model diversity |
| Artifact correction | Same Worker's own approved `file_revise` with latest hash and immutable receipt chain | No general repository editing or predecessor-file mutation |
| Context and memory | Complete bounded source exchange archive/readback, lexical indexes and bounded model semantic source-ID selection | One exploratory cross-language semantic sample is independently interpreted below; no general memory-quality claim |
| Recovery | Durable notice processing, idempotent review/semantic feedback recovery and existing process restart harness | Reopening Store in a fixture does not prove a real mid-execution Core process restart |
| Multimodal | Explicit unsupported/input-needed behavior | Typed image/audio/video ingestion and execution remain unavailable |

The original raw review packet cap is 65,536 bytes. Receipt content, artifacts,
delivery fields and predecessor handoffs are complete; no omitted content or
larger cap is used to create a PASS. A successor must execute its own model,
produce its own result and obtain fresh current verification. Complete validated
predecessor delivery can supply read-only evidence without a fabricated action
receipt or unrelated file read.

The serial policy keeps the original L1/L2/L3 totals of 180,000 / 360,000 /

"""Immutable historical source/test/live boundary without runtime DB access."""

import argparse
import collections
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import re
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import zipfile
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
AUDIT = REPO / "docs/audit/phase2"


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def evidence(path):
    return {
        "path": path.relative_to(REPO).as_posix(),
        "bytes": path.stat().st_size,
        "sha256": sha(path),
    }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--version", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    version = args.version
    if not re.fullmatch(r"v[1-9][0-9]*", version):
        parser.error("version must be v-prefixed positive integer")
    output = AUDIT / f"acceptance-independent-{version}-boundary.json"
    if output.exists() or output.with_suffix(".md").exists():
        raise FileExistsError("Historical boundary outputs are immutable")
    manifest_path = AUDIT / f"source-manifest-{version}.json"
    freeze_path = AUDIT / f"acceptance-independent-{version}-freeze.json"
    usage_path = AUDIT / f"live-usage-{version}-audit.json"
    manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_bytes())
    freeze = json.loads(freeze_path.read_bytes())
    usage = json.loads(usage_path.read_bytes())
    archive = REPO / f".local/phase2/source-snapshot-{version}.zip"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive) as source:
        names = [item.filename for item in source.infolist() if not item.is_dir()]
        expected = {item["path"]: item for item in manifest["files"]}
        differences = []
        for name, item in expected.items():
            if name not in names:
                differences.append({"path": name, "reason": "missing"})
                continue
            raw = source.read(name)
            if (
                len(raw) != item["bytes"]
                or hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() != item["sha256"]
            ):
                differences.append({"path": name, "reason": "hash_or_bytes"})
    extras = sorted(set(names) - set(expected))
    duplicates = [
        name for name, count in collections.Counter(names).items() if count > 1
    ]
    archived = {
        "evidence": evidence(archive),
        "entries": len(names),
        "expected_files": len(expected),
        "differences": differences,
        "extras": extras,
        "duplicates": duplicates,
        "passed": len(names) == len(expected)
        and not differences
        and not extras
        and not duplicates,
    }
    xml_path, log_path = (
        AUDIT / f"frozen-tests-{version}.xml",
        AUDIT / f"frozen-tests-{version}.log",
    )
    xml = ET.parse(xml_path).getroot()
    suites = [xml] if xml.tag == "testsuite" else list(xml.findall("testsuite"))
    cases = list(xml.iter("testcase"))
    identities = [(case.get("classname"), case.get("name")) for case in cases]
    counts = {
        key: sum(int(suite.get(key, 0)) for suite in suites)
        for key in ("tests", "failures", "errors", "skipped")
    }
    summaries = re.findall(
        r"(?m)^.*\b(\d+) passed(?:, (\d+) warning[s]?)? in ([0-9.]+)s",
        log_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
    )
    summary = summaries[-1] if summaries else None
    modules = {
        next(
            (
                part
                for part in case.get("classname", "").split(".")
                if part.startswith("test_")
            ),
            "",
        )
        for case in cases
    }
    expected_modules = {
        Path(name).stem
        for name in expected
        if Path(name).parent.as_posix() == "backend/tests"
        and Path(name).name.startswith("test_")
        and name.endswith(".py")
    }
    tests = {
        "evidence": [evidence(xml_path), evidence(log_path)],
        **counts,
        "testcase_elements": len(cases),
        "console_passed": int(summary[0]) if summary else None,
        "console_warnings": int(summary[1] or 0) if summary else None,
        "console_seconds": float(summary[2]) if summary else None,
        "duplicate_test_identities": [
            list(name)
            for name, count in collections.Counter(identities).items()
            if count > 1
        ],
        "missing_frozen_modules": sorted(expected_modules - modules),
        "extra_junit_modules": sorted(modules - expected_modules),
    }
    tests["passed"] = (
        counts["tests"] == len(cases) == tests["console_passed"]
        and not any(counts[key] for key in ("failures", "errors", "skipped"))
        and not tests["duplicate_test_identities"]
        and not tests["missing_frozen_modules"]
        and not tests["extra_junit_modules"]
    )
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "versioned_auditor", AUDIT / "audit-independent-v17.py"
    )
    auditor = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(auditor)
    auditor.VERSION = version
    static = auditor.static_checks(freeze["source_freeze"])

            for key in (
                "run_id",
                "level",
                "acceptance_status",
                "acceptance_passed",
                "duration_seconds",
                "known_gateway_tokens",
                "missing_gateway_usage_count",
                "final_gateway_state_counts",
                "planner_failure_diagnostics",
            )
        }
        | {
            "worker_runs": len(row["worker_counters"]),
            "retained_planner_rejection_events": len(
                row.get("planner_rejection_events", [])
            ),
        }
        for row in usage["runs"]
    ]
    usage_valid = (
        usage["source_version"] == version
        and usage["frozen_manifest_sha256"] == manifest["manifest_sha256"]
        and all(
            row["frozen_manifest_match"]
            and row["driver_usage_matches_database"]
            and row["accounting_checks_passed"]
            and row["held_allocation_audit"]["passed"]
            and row["read_snapshot_total_changes"] == 0
            and sha(REPO / row["driver_record_path"]) == row["driver_record_sha256"]
            for row in usage["runs"]
        )
    )
    consistent = (
        archived["passed"]
        and tests["passed"]
        and all(row["passed"] for row in static)
        and freeze["checks_passed"]
        and usage_valid
    )
    report = {
        "generated_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
        "source_version": version,
        "status": "historical_failed_boundary",
        "phase2_complete": False,
        "scope": "Historical frozen suite and strict live failures. Archived source is rehashed without extracting or treating it as current source. No tests, Provider calls, Store construction, credentials or runtime database access.",
        "boundary_auditor": evidence(Path(__file__).resolve()),
        "source_manifest": evidence(manifest_path),
        "canonical_manifest_sha256": manifest["manifest_sha256"],
        "original_frozen_observation": evidence(freeze_path),
        "captured_source_static_preservation_passed": freeze["checks_passed"],
        "historical_source_archive": archived,
        "full_tests": tests,
        "static_checks": static,
        "preservation": freeze["preservation"],
        "usage_audit": evidence(usage_path),

"""Explicit Core sizing measures resources, never supplies a semantic plan."""

import copy
import json

import pytest
from test_planner_capacity_v17 import handoff_graph
from test_router_intelligence_phase2 import ScriptedMock
from test_verified_capacity_v16 import generate, prepared

from forge_core.capacity_preflight import verified_input_inventory
from forge_core.domain import DomainError
from forge_core.graph_domain import CapacityGraphWire
from forge_core.provider_pool import ProviderPool
from forge_core.providers import ProviderConfig, ProviderGateway
from forge_core.quest_graph import QuestGraphService
from forge_core.team_composition import TeamCompositionService


class NativeFramingMock(ProviderGateway):
    """Mock output plus production native serializer; no network calls."""

    def __init__(self, graph):
        super().__init__(
            ProviderConfig(
                id="p",
                kind="openai_compatible",
                base_url="https://example.invalid/v1",
                credential_ref="FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_TEST",
                supports_tools=True,
                supports_json_schema=True,
            )
        )
        self.graph = graph
        self.requests = []

    async def generate(self, request):
        self.requests.append(request)
        return type("MockResponse", (), {"text": json.dumps(self.graph), "usage": {}})()


def measured_graph():
    graph = handoff_graph()
    graph["allocation_mode"] = "core_measured_serial"
    graph["serial_capacity_policy"] = None
    # Deliberately impossible guesses: only explicit Core mode may replace them.
    for node in graph["nodes"]:
        node["budget_tokens"] = 900000
    return graph


def prepared_chain(tmp_path):
    return prepared(
        tmp_path,
        content='Assess inputs/unicode.json. Task execution limits: {"max_total_tokens":360000,"max_nodes":2,"max_members":2}',
    )


def test_explicit_native_sizing_preserves_every_semantic_field_and_needs_approval(tmp_path):
    store, quest = prepared_chain(tmp_path)
    graph = measured_graph()
    provider = NativeFramingMock(graph)
    before = copy.deepcopy(graph)
    plan = generate(store, quest, provider)
    assert graph == before
    assert len(provider.requests) == 1
    assert plan["status"] == "proposed"
    assert store.get_quest(quest.id)["status"] != "approved"
    assert plan["edges"] == graph["edges"]
    for node, expected in zip(plan["nodes"], graph["nodes"], strict=True):
        expected = {
            **expected,
            "required_capabilities": {
                item["name"]: item["minimum"] for item in expected["required_capabilities"]
            },
        }
        actual = {key: node[key] for key in expected if key != "budget_tokens"}
        assert actual == {key: value for key, value in expected.items() if key != "budget_tokens"}
        assert (
            node["budget_tokens"]
            == plan["capacity_contract"]["nodes"][node["key"]]["initial_work_tokens"] + 4096
        )
    shared = plan["serial_capacity_policy"]["shared_reserve_tokens"]
    assert shared == max(
        item["minimum_node_tokens"]
        - item["initial_work_tokens"]
        + (2 + item["review_envelope"]["correction_calls"]) * 4096
        for item in plan["capacity_contract"]["nodes"].values()
    )
    assert (
        sum(node["budget_tokens"] for node in plan["nodes"])
        + shared
        + plan["coordination_reserve_tokens"]
        <= graph["max_total_tokens"]
    )
    provenance = plan["capacity_contract"]["resource_allocation"]
    assert provenance["fixed_point_verified"] is True
    assert 2 <= provenance["iterations"] <= 8
    assert all(
        item["initial_worker_request_measurement"]["native_input_reservation"] > 0
        for item in plan["capacity_contract"]["nodes"].values()
    )
    with store.connection() as connection:
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM worker_runs").fetchone()[0] == 0
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM action_receipts").fetchone()[0] == 0


@pytest.mark.parametrize("mutation", ["total", "raw_packet", "context", "branch", "legacy"])
def test_impossible_measured_semantics_are_rejected_without_changing_bounds(tmp_path, mutation):
    store, quest = prepared_chain(tmp_path)
    graph = measured_graph()
    if mutation == "total":
        graph.update(max_total_tokens=30000, coordination_reserve_tokens=3000)
    elif mutation == "raw_packet":
        graph["nodes"][0]["capacity_bounds"]["max_source_receipt_bytes"] = 65536
    elif mutation == "context":
        profile = store.list_models()[0]
        profile.context_window = 4096
        store.save_model(profile)
    elif mutation == "branch":
        graph["edges"] = []
    else:
        graph["allocation_mode"] = "model_declared"
    before = copy.deepcopy(graph)
    provider = ScriptedMock(graph)
    with pytest.raises(DomainError, match="Invalid graph proposal"):
        generate(store, quest, provider)
    assert len(provider.requests) == 2
    assert graph == before
    assert QuestGraphService(store).history(quest.id) == []


def test_measured_wire_cannot_skip_runtime_resource_quantification():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="native capacity measurement"):
        CapacityGraphWire.model_validate(measured_graph()).proposal()


def test_actual_team_contract_is_remeasured_with_approved_role_cycle_headroom(tmp_path):

def _planning_limits(operator_max_total_tokens=None):
    if operator_max_total_tokens is not None and (
        type(operator_max_total_tokens) is not int or operator_max_total_tokens < 1
    ):
        raise ValueError("Operator max total tokens must be a positive integer")
    maximum = (
        1000000 if operator_max_total_tokens is None else min(1000000, operator_max_total_tokens)
    )
    return {
        "max_nodes": 8,
        "max_edges": 16,
        "max_total_tokens": maximum,
        "node_budget_tokens_max": maximum,
        "success_criteria_per_node": "1-5",
        "depth": "flat or shallow; prefer 2-4 sequential nodes",
    }


def _admit_planner_request(provider, request):
    """Check the complete request, including policy and schema, before any call."""
    from .providers import ProviderError, ProviderGateway, schema_format_instruction

    if isinstance(provider, ProviderGateway):
        try:
            provider._payload(request, False)
        except ProviderError as exc:
            if exc.code == "context_exceeded":
                raise DomainError("Planner context budget exceeded") from None
            raise
        return
    # Explicit non-native adapters/Mock protocols retain conservative framing.
    # The actual native Gateway always takes the exact serializer branch above.
    messages = list(request.messages)
    schema = request.response_format["json_schema"]["schema"]
    messages.insert(1, {"role": "system", "content": schema_format_instruction(schema)})
    payload = {
        "model": request.model_id,
        "messages": messages,
        "response_format": request.response_format,
        "max_tokens": request.max_output_tokens,
        "stream": False,
    }
    size = len(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")) + 64
    if size + request.max_output_tokens > request.context_limit:
        raise DomainError("Planner context budget exceeded")


def _validation_digest(exc):
    """Bounded, non-sensitive summary of a rejected proposal."""
    if isinstance(exc, ValidationError):
        items = []
        for error in exc.errors()[:3]:
            location = ".".join(str(part) for part in error.get("loc", ()))
            items.append((location + ": " + str(error.get("msg", "")))[:200])
        return items or ["validation_failed"]
    return [str(exc)[:200]]


def _canonical(value):
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))

function Replace-StageText([string]$Name, [string]$Old, [string]$New) {
    $taskPath = Join-Path $taskStage $Name

    if (-not $taskText.Contains($Old)) { throw "Missing expected text in $Name" }

}

composition, not success under the current measured contracts.

## Exact-plan counterfactual measurement

The current native envelope was measured without executing a team or model.
The replay uses the actual persisted node, source inventory and model profile,
the full node objective and path contract, and otherwise identical role fields.
`resource_sizing=True` reports the complete requirement without admitting it.

tokens: one initial output and one correction output each add 6,144. Selecting
the instructed strict output schema adds another 588 in this fixed contract.

does not prove that any particular rejected real response made that choice.
There is no necessary baseline/pool/coordination contradiction: smaller complete
role contracts and the measured output ceiling fit the approved allocation.

1. Add an explicit native Composer semantic wire. The model chooses role
   identity/specialization, task-node binding and bounded semantic contracts.
   Keep the legacy manual TeamWire and API unchanged. Do not accept model-written
   resource fields in the new wire.
2. Core binds each pending role's cumulative allocation to its approved node
   baseline. Bind the per-call output ceiling to the approved profile-specific
   measurement (the saved initial output reservation and matching correction
   output, 2,048 for this plan); calculate `input_tokens = baseline - output`
   once. Validate nonnegative input and the selected model's output/context
   limits. Preserve the complete delivery bound; a small output ceiling must
   fail honestly if it cannot return the required full result.
3. Measure the same default strict eight-field schema in Planner and Composer.
   Preserve full role responsibility/input/criteria in actual team remeasurement.
   A finite role-framing allowance is not permission to skip that check. If a
   different profile, custom schema or semantic contract does not fit, reject
   with a typed capacity diagnostic instead of raising a budget or changing
   source/output bounds.
4. Core derives the concrete team ceiling from pending baselines plus the serial
   shared reserve once. Concurrency remains one for serial policy; all other
   concurrency, member, depth, step, tool, duration and cost limits remain within
   the original task/operator constraints. Core should allocate finite role
   durations with their sum within the approved total, preserving any explicit
   user requirement. The model need not repeat these additions or subtractions.
5. Keep the existing selected-Provider native preflight, held/residual budget
   checks and normal plan/team approval. The L1 snapshot already spent its
   coordination budget on repeated failed composition, so a repair cannot reuse
   this run as though those charges were refunded.
6. Stop deterministic team-contract rejection after one correction round with a
   preserved bounded rejection event and exact response hash, as Planner does.
   Keep transport/unknown/concurrency handling separate. Do not infer or refund
   an external attempt. Preserve the original failed V20 database and run.

Passing contract tests after this change would not establish real model quality
or Phase 2 completion. Fresh frozen-source strict L1/L2/L3 runs remain required,
with the original 180k / 360k / 630k caps, full 65,536-byte raw review limit,
actual artifacts, independent verification and required mid-execution continuity.

"""A stopped team proposal is a failure; active notices keep the driver waiting."""

import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from test_driver_terminal_planning_v19 import database


@pytest.fixture
def driver():
    path = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "scripts/phase2/live_e2e.py"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("driver_terminal_composition_v21", path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def test_terminal_composition_is_read_only_and_retains_attempts(tmp_path, driver):
    target = database(
        tmp_path,
        [
            ("failed", "composer", "q", None, 1, "composition_failed:InvalidTeamProposal", 1.0),
            ("planner", "planner", "q", None, 1, None, None),
            ("other", "composer", "other", None, 1, None, None),
            ("processed", "composer", "q", "done", 1, None, None),
        ],
    )
    original = target.read_bytes()
    result = driver.terminal_composition_failure(tmp_path, "q")
    assert result["status"] == "failed"
    assert result["reason"] == "all_composer_notices_terminal"
    assert result["read_only_changes"] == 0
    assert [row["event_id"] for row in result["notices"]] == ["failed"]
    assert result["notices"][0]["notice_attempts"] == 1
    assert target.read_bytes() == original


@pytest.mark.parametrize("active_error", [None, "composition_failed:retrying"])
def test_active_composer_notice_prevents_early_failure(tmp_path, driver, active_error):

        tmp_path,
        [
            ("old", "composer", "q", None, 1, "composition_failed:InvalidTeamProposal", 1.0),
            ("active", "composer", "q", None, 1, active_error, None),
        ],
    )
    assert driver.terminal_composition_failure(tmp_path, "q") is None


def test_transport_dead_letter_is_not_a_deterministic_team_rejection(tmp_path, driver):
    database(tmp_path, [("network", "composer", "q", None, 5, "resource_busy", 1.0)])
    assert driver.terminal_composition_failure(tmp_path, "q") is None


def test_missing_database_remains_absent(tmp_path, driver):

    assert not (tmp_path / "data").exists()

"""Production Composer semantics bound to previously approved Core resources.

This adapter proposes no permissions, changes no plan, and performs no model
selection. TeamCompositionService must still validate the resulting proposal,
remeasure the selected Provider request, and require normal user approval.
Legacy TeamWire and manual proposal callers retain their original allocations.
"""

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from .budget_policy import validate_serial_policy
from .domain import DomainError
from .hierarchical_plans import node_depth
from .team_composition import TeamCapabilityWire, TeamWire


class InvalidTeamProposal(DomainError):
    """Two settled production Composer responses failed deterministic admission."""


def uses_core_composer_resources(graph):
    contract = graph.get("capacity_contract") or {}
    return (
        contract.get("version") == "verified-capacity-v1"
        and (contract.get("resource_allocation") or {}).get("mode") == "core_measured"
        and bool(contract.get("nodes"))
        and all(
            type(item.get("output_bound")) is int and item["output_bound"] > 0
            for item in contract["nodes"].values()
        )
    )


class SemanticTeamRoleWire(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    id: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)
    task_node_key: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)
    required_capabilities: list[TeamCapabilityWire] = Field(max_length=32)
    tools: list[str] = Field(max_length=32)
    dynamic: bool
    responsibility: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=2000)
    input_contract: list[str] = Field(max_length=20)
    output_schema_json: str | None = Field(
        description="Explicit null selects the supplied Core strict eight-field delivery schema."
    )
    acceptance_criteria: list[str] = Field(max_length=20)


class SemanticTeamWire(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    roles: list[SemanticTeamRoleWire] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=16)
    strategy: Literal["single_model", "greedy", "coverage", "complementarity"]

    def inputs(self, graph, *, operator_max_concurrency):
        """Bind exact approved output/baseline; normal service admission follows.

        Source limits remain ceilings. Steps/tools use bounded Core defaults when
        no source limit exists; duration is divided within the approved total.
        The shared serial reserve appears once in the team limit and never in
        role allocations. Execution limits remain the service's responsibility.
        """
        if not uses_core_composer_resources(graph):
            raise DomainError("Core Composer requires approved measured output bounds")
        if type(operator_max_concurrency) is not int or operator_max_concurrency < 1:
            raise DomainError("Core Composer requires an operator concurrency ceiling")
        nodes = {node["key"]: node for node in graph["nodes"]}
        keys = [role.task_node_key for role in self.roles]
        if len(set(keys)) != len(keys) or set(keys) - set(nodes):
            raise DomainError("Each approved task node requires exactly one team member")
        maximum = (graph.get("execution_constraints") or {}).get("limits", {})
        count = len(self.roles)
        if count > min(16, maximum.get("max_members", 16)):
            raise DomainError("Team max_members exceeds source-bound task limit")
        serial = validate_serial_policy(graph)
        concurrency = (
            1
            if serial
            else min(count, operator_max_concurrency, maximum.get("max_concurrency", count))
        )
        duration = min(
            graph.get("max_duration_seconds") or 120 * count,
            maximum.get("max_duration_seconds", 120 * count),
            3600 * count,
        )
        if type(duration) is not int or duration < count:
            raise DomainError("Approved duration cannot fund every team member")
        per_role_duration, extra = divmod(duration, count)
        duration_by_key = {
            key: per_role_duration + (index < extra) for index, key in enumerate(sorted(keys))
        }
        steps = min(32, maximum.get("max_worker_steps", 16))
        calls = min(64, maximum.get("max_worker_tool_calls", 16))
        roles = []
        observations = graph["capacity_contract"]["nodes"]
        for wire in self.roles:
            node = nodes[wire.task_node_key]
            output = observations.get(wire.task_node_key, {}).get("output_bound")
            baseline = node["budget_tokens"]
            if type(output) is not int or not 0 < output < baseline:
                raise DomainError("Approved measured output cannot fit its node baseline")
            roles.append(
                {
                    **wire.model_dump(),
                    "input_tokens": baseline - output,
                    "output_tokens": output,
                    "max_steps": steps,
                    "max_tool_calls": calls if wire.tools else 0,
                    "max_duration_seconds": duration_by_key[wire.task_node_key],
                    "depth": node_depth(graph, wire.task_node_key),
                }
            )
        allocation = sum(nodes[key]["budget_tokens"] for key in keys) + (
            serial["shared_reserve_tokens"] if serial else 0
        )
        if allocation > min(
            graph["max_total_tokens"] - (graph.get("coordination_reserve_tokens") or 0),
            maximum.get("max_total_tokens", graph["max_total_tokens"]),
        ):
            raise DomainError("Core team resources exceed the original approved ceiling")
        tools = sorted({tool for role in self.roles for tool in role.tools})
        limits = {
            "max_members": count,
            "max_depth": max(role["depth"] for role in roles),
            "max_concurrency": concurrency,
            "max_total_tokens": allocation,
            "max_total_tool_calls": sum(role["max_tool_calls"] for role in roles),
            "max_cost_microunits": graph.get("max_cost_microunits"),
            "currency": graph.get("cost_currency"),
            "allowed_tools": tools,
        }
        # The unchanged legacy parser supplies all established role validators,
        # including explicit-null strict schema selection for dynamic roles.
        return TeamWire.model_validate(
            {"roles": roles, "limits": limits, "strategy": self.strategy}
        ).inputs()


_DIAGNOSTIC_FIELDS = frozenset(
    {
        "roles",
        "id",
        "task_node_key",
        "required_capabilities",
        "name",
        "minimum",
        "tools",
        "dynamic",
        "responsibility",
        "input_contract",
        "output_schema_json",
        "acceptance_criteria",
        "strategy",
        "limits",
        "input_tokens",
        "output_tokens",
        "max_steps",
        "max_tool_calls",
        "max_duration_seconds",
        "depth",
        "max_members",
        "max_depth",
        "max_concurrency",
        "max_total_tokens",
        "max_total_tool_calls",
        "max_cost_microunits",
        "currency",
        "allowed_tools",
    }
)
_CAPACITY_NUMBERS = frozenset(
    {
        "known_source_bytes",
        "future_source_bytes_bound",
        "raw_packet_bytes",
        "growth_bound",
        "raw_packet_bound",
        "raw_packet_limit",
        "review_input_bound",
        "correction_input_bound",
        "worker_input_bound",
        "model_context_limit",
        "output_bound",
        "allocated_tokens",
        "minimum_node_tokens",
        "review_correction_reserve",
        "initial_work_tokens",
        "baseline_tokens",
    }
)


def safe_team_rejection_diagnostics(exc=None):
    """No model text, input values, exception messages, or raw schemas are stored."""
    result = {"kind": "incomplete_team_proposal" if exc is None else "invalid_team_proposal"}
    errors = getattr(exc, "errors", None)
    if callable(errors):
        result["fields"] = [
            [
                part
                if type(part) is int and 0 <= part <= 127
                else part
                if isinstance(part, str) and part in _DIAGNOSTIC_FIELDS
                else "unrecognized_field"
                for part in error.get("loc", ())[:8]
            ]
            for error in errors()[:8]
        ]
    capacity = getattr(exc, "capacity_diagnostics", None)
    if isinstance(capacity, dict):
        result["capacity"] = {
            key: value
            for key, value in capacity.items()
            if key in _CAPACITY_NUMBERS and type(value) is int and 0 <= value <= 1000000000
        }
    return result

def semantic_team(graph):
    return {
        "roles": [
            {
                "id": "research" if index == 0 else "reviewer",
                "task_node_key": node["key"],
                "required_capabilities": [
                    {"name": name, "minimum": value}
                    for name, value in node["required_capabilities"].items()
                ],
                "tools": node["allowed_tools"],
                "dynamic": False,
                "responsibility": "Inspect approved sources",
                "input_contract": node["required_input_paths"] or ["Approved objective"],
                "output_schema_json": None,
                "acceptance_criteria": node["success_criteria"],
            }
            for index, node in enumerate(graph["nodes"])
        ],
        "strategy": "greedy",
    }


def graph_fixture(*, serial=False):
    nodes = [
        {
            "key": key,
            "budget_tokens": 150000,
            "required_capabilities": {},
            "required_input_paths": [],
            "allowed_tools": ["file_read"],
            "success_criteria": ["delivery_review"],
        }
        for key in (["a", "b"] if serial else ["a"])
    ]
    graph = {
        "nodes": nodes,
        "edges": [{"source": "a", "target": "b", "condition": "success"}] if serial else [],
        "max_total_tokens": 400000,
        "max_duration_seconds": 300,
        "coordination_reserve_tokens": 40000,
        "execution_constraints": {
            "limits": {
                "max_members": 2,
                "max_concurrency": 2,
                "max_worker_steps": 12,
                "max_worker_tool_calls": 7,
                "max_duration_seconds": 250,
            }
        },
        "capacity_contract": {
            "version": "verified-capacity-v1",
            "resource_allocation": {"mode": "core_measured"},
            "nodes": {node["key"]: {"output_bound": 2048} for node in nodes},
        },
    }
    if serial:
        graph["serial_capacity_policy"] = {
            "version": "serial-capacity-v1",
            "shared_reserve_tokens": 50000,
        }
    return graph


def test_strict_semantic_schema_has_no_numeric_resource_fields():
    schema = SemanticTeamWire.model_json_schema()
    assert set(schema["properties"]) == {"roles", "strategy"}
    properties = schema["$defs"]["SemanticTeamRoleWire"]["properties"]
    assert not {
        "input_tokens",
        "output_tokens",
        "max_steps",
        "max_tool_calls",
        "max_duration_seconds",
        "depth",
    } & set(properties)
    for item in [schema, *schema["$defs"].values()]:
        if item.get("type") == "object":
            assert set(item["required"]) == set(item["properties"])


@pytest.mark.parametrize("serial", [False, True])
def test_core_binds_exact_approved_resources_without_mutating_semantics(serial):
    graph = graph_fixture(serial=serial)
    proposal = semantic_team(graph)
    before = copy.deepcopy((graph, proposal))
    jsonschema.validate(proposal, SemanticTeamWire.model_json_schema())
    roles, limits, strategy = SemanticTeamWire.model_validate(proposal).inputs(
        graph, operator_max_concurrency=1
    )
    assert (graph, proposal) == before
    assert strategy == "greedy" and limits.max_concurrency == 1
    for role, wire in zip(roles, proposal["roles"], strict=True):
        assert role.input_tokens == 147952 and role.output_tokens == 2048
        assert role.input_tokens + role.output_tokens == 150000
        assert role.max_steps == 12 and role.max_tool_calls == 7
        assert role.tools == wire["tools"]
        assert role.acceptance_criteria == wire["acceptance_criteria"]
        assert role.input_contract == wire["input_contract"]
        assert role.output_schema == STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA
    assert sum(role.max_duration_seconds for role in roles) == 250
    assert limits.max_total_tokens == 150000 * len(roles) + (50000 if serial else 0)
    assert limits.max_total_tool_calls == 7 * len(roles)

def test_semantic_model_cannot_override_core_resource_numbers(field):

    proposal["roles"][0][field] = 8192
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):

def test_legacy_wire_preserves_model_submitted_allocations():
    proposal = team_wire()
    roles, limits, _ = TeamWire.model_validate(proposal).inputs()
    assert roles[0].input_tokens == 100 and roles[0].output_tokens == 50
    assert limits.max_total_tokens == 150
    for mode in [None, "model_declared", "core_measured_serial"]:
        graph = graph_fixture()
        graph["capacity_contract"]["resource_allocation"]["mode"] = mode
        assert not uses_core_composer_resources(graph)


def test_remaining_contract_binds_only_unfinished_nodes_without_legacy_fallback():
    graph = graph_fixture(serial=True)
    del graph["capacity_contract"]["nodes"]["a"]
    proposal = semantic_team(graph)
    proposal["roles"] = [role for role in proposal["roles"] if role["task_node_key"] == "b"]
    before = copy.deepcopy(graph)
    assert uses_core_composer_resources(graph)
    roles, limits, _ = SemanticTeamWire.model_validate(proposal).inputs(
        graph, operator_max_concurrency=2
    )
    assert [role.task_node_key for role in roles] == ["b"]
    assert roles[0].input_tokens + roles[0].output_tokens == 150000
    assert limits.max_total_tokens == 200000 and limits.max_concurrency == 1
    assert graph == before

def test_safe_diagnostics_do_not_persist_exception_or_unknown_field_values():
    marker = "PRIVATE_SOURCE_AND_SECRET_MARKER"
    proposal = semantic_team(graph_fixture())
    proposal["roles"][0][marker] = marker
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError) as caught:

    diagnostic = safe_team_rejection_diagnostics(caught.value)
    assert marker not in json.dumps(diagnostic)
    assert diagnostic["fields"] == [["roles", 0, "unrecognized_field"]]
    assert len(json.dumps(diagnostic).encode()) < 4096


def test_safe_capacity_diagnostics_retain_only_whitelisted_nonnegative_integers():
    marker = "PRIVATE_SOURCE_AND_SECRET_MARKER"

tools.name: exec

tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.
tools.name: wait

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.

        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

tools.name: mcp__cua_repl

tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

On Windows, choose the requested window by app and title from the inventory. Pass the selected window's ID as returned.

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp({ windowId: selected.id });
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, make your next tool call `cua_repl.js` with only `completion_summary`, exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- When presenting media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to bypass the app's restrictions on presenting it to the user.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- When you write or rewrite an automation prompt, keep it within 10,000 estimated tokens.
- When the user asks to manage an app automation, set a reminder, or schedule a recurring task, use the relevant Automations action to help the user. Do not write raw automation directives by hand.
- Create an automation when the user wants a reminder, a recurring report, or a standing alert for future events.
- Do not create an automation to track a specific job or task through a milestone, failure, or completion. If the user asks you to watch a run or task to completion, keep checking in the current task and follow through when the requested condition is met.
- Unless the user asks for periodic updates, notify them only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action.
- When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, permanently delete, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, `delete_thread`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
